_comment: McAllen-Edinburg-Mission, TX MSA — Hidalgo County. Ingested from the ChatGPT Work research workbook 2026-08-03 as part of wave 1 of the v2.0 methodology. NOT YET IMPORTED. `expected_publish` is deliberately ABSENT: for a new metro the projected split IS the finding the owner needs, so it is reported by --stage=project rather than asserted. Once the owner approves the split, record it here so the real import run re-asserts it.
_workbook_comment: Research methodology v2.0 — the tab override is load-bearing. v2.0 splits the human research artifact from the machine handoff: the 15 human tabs are unchanged and a new generated `Import Contract` tab is now the ONLY machine input. This workbook is generation A by tab layout, so detectGeneration() would read generation A's default primary tab `Import Ready`, which v2.0 demotes to a human-readable view. Reading a human tab as machine input is the Huntsville defect class. applyTabOverrides() ABORTS on a missing named tab rather than falling back silently.
_envelope_comment: Derived from the MSA COUNTY LIST, not the observed venue bbox (Toledo precedent). The McAllen-Edinburg-Mission MSA is coextensive with Hidalgo County, so the envelope is Hidalgo County's own extent rounded OUTWARD to 0.01 deg. Extent from the US Census TIGERweb State_County service: lat 26.036268..26.783081, lng -98.586444..-97.861684. NOTE THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER: Hidalgo County's southern edge is the Rio Grande, and the envelope's latMin therefore sits on the Mexican border. `states: [TX]` is the independent fence that rejects any non-Texas row, so a Reynosa-side venue cannot enter on geography alone — belt and braces, not one or the other.
_geocode_comment: 26 of 30 venues geocoded (19 high precision, 7 low) — the WORST low-precision rate in wave 1, and the cause is structural rather than random. Most of this metro's held rows are RV resorts and 55+ active-adult communities, which OSM largely holds as named areas without house numbers, so the structured rung lands on the access road instead of the venue ('1015-rv-park' anchored to International Boulevard; 'paradise-resort-estates' to East Hall Acres Road). That is repair-pass class 1a — these need a better ANCHOR, not a better address, and a name-anchored Overpass query inside the envelope is the cheap fix. Four produce no coordinate at all (incredibowl-pickle-padel, pharr-development-research-center, llano-grande-resort, trails-end-rv-resort). Every miss is a genuine HTTP 200 with an empty result set, not rate limiting — scripts/lib/geocode-nominatim.mjs throws on any non-200. Set false so these import as gate-blocked drafts instead of aborting the metro. NOTE: geocoding is NOT this metro's binding constraint — 23 of 30 rows are research_status=probable and would be held on the evidence bar even with a perfect coordinate.
_expected_publish_comment: The projected split as APPROVED BY THE OWNER on 2026-08-03, recorded so --stage=project and --stage=publish both re-assert it and fail the run on any divergence. If a later run disagrees with this block, fix the pipeline or the data — never edit this block to match the output. OWNER DECISION on the 20% rate: this metro ships at 6 of 30 rather than waiting for a Pass-2 verification run. The 24 held rows import as drafts and stay off the site, so holding the whole metro would delay 6 controlling-entity-verified venues for the sake of 24 that need per-row research either way. 18 of the 24 are RV resorts and 55+ active-adult communities, which have no controlling-entity web presence to find — Pass 2 on this metro is expected to be low-yield and should be scheduled on that basis.
